papers.title: From T-cell renewal to immune longevity: a multilevel capacity framework for immune aging.
papers.authors: Li H, Zhi Y.
papers.abstract: Consider what the T-cell compartment accomplishes. For decades it sustains immune competence while the thymus shrinks, antigens accumulate, and tissues change around it. We propose that this longevity rests on four coupled capacities: input renewal, repertoire maintenance and clonal dynamics, lineage-constrained plasticity, and tissue-contextual fitness. Input renewal is treated as a proxy domain inferred from calibrated peripheral correlates, not as a direct measure of thymic flux. Our claim is simple: these capacities need not age in concert, whether one compares individuals, tissues, or challenges. The biology behind them is well known. Thymic involution restricts the entry of naive T cells, antigen history reshapes the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, metabolic and epigenetic changes erode proliferative reserve, and aged tissue niches alter survival, trafficking, and local function. Nevertheless, some individuals retain protective responses in particular subsets and tissues, a pattern consistent with compensation during aging and exceptional longevity. We introduce renewable potential as a broader concept than T-cell stemness and distinguish terminal differentiation from exhaustion and senescence-like phenotypes. We then consider how longitudinal turnover measurements, clone-aware analyses, and perturbation studies can move the field beyond cross-sectional, age-associated signatures. Its predictions are concrete: capacities may disagree within a person, compartments may age at different rates, the limiting capacity may depend on context, compensation may give way to maladaptive fixation, and intervention responses may vary with the baseline capacity profile. Vaccination and infection, cancer, transplantation, autoimmunity, and tissue inflammation illustrate these constraints. On this view, the T-cell immune-longevity capacity profile describes a context-dependent pattern of deficits and compensations, not a universal immune-age score or a proxy for chronological age.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis reveals transcriptomic patterns in active macrophage activation syndrome and therapeutic potential of albumin-fused interleukin-10 in a mouse model.
papers.authors: Fujii W, Sofue H, Yuba E, Ishihara J, Baßler K, Hasegawa A, Hiyama T, Komatsu S, Nakamura K, Tanaka A, Arai S, Maezawa R, Arima M, Kurasawa K, Owada T, Kamitsuji Y, Uoshima N, Kobayashi T, Uchiyama H, Mizutani S, Kuroda J, Kawahito Y, Ikeda K.
papers.abstract: Introduction Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) are life-threatening hyperinflammatory conditions. We aimed to characterize immune cell transcriptomic patterns in human MAS and investigate the therapeutic potential of albumin-fused IL-10 protein (SA-IL-10) in a MAS mouse model. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on bone marrow and peripheral blood samples from patients with newly developed MAS caused by diverse etiologies. We generated paired Seq-Well single-cell transcriptomes from bone marrow and blood of patients with active HLH/MAS. In the absence of a contemporaneous control cohort, technology-matched public Seq-Well marrow and same-laboratory control blood were projected onto the frozen patient atlases as lineage context, not as a case-control comparison. We also evaluated the effect of SA-IL-10 in a CpG-DNA-induced mouse model of MAS. Results Human scRNA-seq identified diverse immune cell populations, including dendritic cells, macrophages, and monocyte subsets. Canonical lineages in the public data were transferred to the expected patient states. Monocyte 1 and macrophage populations expressed transcripts encoding IL-10 receptor subunits and associated signaling molecules, although these findings reflect RNA abundance and do not establish functional responsiveness. Donor-level phagocytosis and interferon-γ programs showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction. In the mouse model, SA-IL-10 treatment significantly improved anemia, leukocytopenia, splenomegaly, and liver dysfunction and was associated with reduced circulating interferon-γ levels and bone marrow macrophage abundance. Conclusion Human scRNA-seq provides transcriptomic patterns in active HLH/MAS. The therapeutic effects observed in the mouse model support further investigation of SA-IL-10 as a potential treatment for MAS.

papers.title: A single-cell atlas of uterosacral ligaments reveals progressive cellular remodeling in pelvic organ prolapse.
papers.authors: Liu L, Hao Y, Deng X, Li L, Chen X, Zhao X, Wang Q, Zhang P.
papers.abstract: Background Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disorder of pelvic support tissues, but its cellular basis in the uterosacral ligament (USL) remains poorly defined. Most existing single-cell studies, have failed to characterize stage-specific cellular changes across different POP severities, lacking a stage-resolved perspective across disease severity stages. Methods We profiled USL samples from 10 women with POP (4 moderate, 6 severe) and 4 controls by single-cell RNA sequencing, and analyzed 167,609 high-quality cells using clustering, trajectory inference, differential expression, cell-cell communication, and transcription factor analyses to systematically decode progressive USL cellular alterations. Results Ten major cell populations were identified. Fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells (SMCs), and endothelial cells formed the structural core of the USL, while macrophages, neutrophils, mast cells, and T cells showed progressive inflammatory activation with increasing disease severity. Fibroblasts were highly heterogeneous and shifted from progenitor-like and perivascular states toward inflammatory, matrix-remodeling, and myofibroblast-like phenotypes. SMCs moved from a contractile program to stress-responsive and ECM-remodeling states, and endothelial cells underwent functional reprogramming rather than major compositional change. Cell-cell communication between stromal cells declined, whereas fibroblast-immune interactions increased. Collagen-related signaling decreased, while immune-associated ligand-receptor programs became more prominent as disease advanced. Conclusion Distinct from previous cross-sectional single-cell studies on POP, this work provides a unique stage-resolved transcriptomic landscape covering moderate-to-severe POP stages. POP is marked by coordinated stromal remodeling, immune activation, and disrupted intercellular signaling in the USL. This single-cell transcriptomic atlas provides a refined framework for interpreting stage-specific molecular alterations across graded POP severities and may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for pelvic floor dysfunction.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Spatiotemporal remodeling of the tumor-immune interface during neoadjuvant immunotherapy for oral squamous cell carcinoma: pathological response, resistance, and dynamic biomarkers.
papers.authors: Xue J, Jia T, Yu J, Wang S, Liang J.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is locally aggressive and frequently associated with cervical lymph-node metastasis and postoperative recurrence. Recent clinical advances in perioperative immunotherapy have made the neoadjuvant setting an important window for investigating dynamic changes in the tumor-immune microenvironment under therapeutic pressure. However, pathological responses vary substantially among patients, and baseline biomarkers such as the PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) and tumor mutational burden (TMB) do not reliably identify those most likely to benefit. Evidence from single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, multiplex imaging, and longitudinal liquid-biopsy studies indicates that pathological response is closely associated with antigen presentation, expansion-competent T cells, tertiary lymphoid structures, vascular routes of immune-cell entry, and myeloid-stromal remodeling. In contrast, impaired antigen presentation, T-cell exclusion, immunosuppressive macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, hypoxic metabolism, and lymph-node-specific niches are associated with residual resistance. This review examines spatiotemporal changes at the tumor-immune interface before and after neoadjuvant immunotherapy for OSCC, with an emphasis on pathological response, mechanisms of resistance, and dynamic biomarkers. We also discuss the translational potential of these features for patient stratification and perioperative treatment decision-making.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing delineates compositional and transcriptional changes of porcine peripheral blood mononuclear cell populations following Salmonella I 4,[5],12:i:- inoculation.
papers.authors: Meeks-Patience CS, Kapoor M, Byrne KA, Anderson CL, Dekkers JCM, Loving CL, Tuggle CK.
papers.abstract: A major contributor to foodborne illnesses worldwide is non-typhoidal Salmonella enterica . Consumption of contaminated pork products is a leading cause of salmonellosis, and understanding porcine cell type-specific immune response to Salmonella may provide information to reduce the Salmonella burden in pigs and conversely reduce the risk of salmonellosis in humans. Five young pigs were inoculated with Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar I 4,[5],12:i:-. Blood was collected at 0, 2, and 8 days post-inoculation (DPI) to assess leukocyte populations in whole blood and isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on PBMCs to interrogate gene expression and compositional changes through the acute stage following inoculation. Eight major immune cell types were identified, and differences in gene expression and cell abundance were assessed for each cell type. A whole-blood flow cytometry assay was performed to determine the proportion and concentration of specific immune cell types. Our findings indicated an increase in circulating monocytes at 2 DPI, including a distinct cluster of intermediate monocytes with increased expression of genes in inflammatory and antibacterial pathways. Major differences in natural killer cell gene expression were detected at 8 DPI compared to 0 DPI. Further, natural killer cells had distinct subsets representing effector and migratory cell states. Collectively, these discoveries unveil the acute, circulating cell type-specific immune response following Salmonella inoculation of pigs.

papers.title: NOTCH3/JAG1 signaling is associated with immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment features in ovarian cancer: links to nutritional risk, CD163+ macrophages, and CD8+ T cell exclusion.
papers.authors: Zhu H, He Y, Hao R, Li X, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Background NOTCH3 signaling is frequently dysregulated in ovarian cancer and has been linked to tumor progression and treatment resistance. We investigated the prognostic significance of NOTCH3 expression and its associations with immune-cell infiltration, nutritional risk, tumor-associated biomarkers, and transcriptional programs in public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 186 patients with epithelial ovarian cancer stratified by immunohistochemistry-assessed NOTCH3 expression ( n = 93 per group). Clinicopathological variables, nutritional measures (BMI, serum albumin, and NRS-2002), tumor-associated biomarkers (CA-125 and HE4), immune markers (CD8+, CD4+, CD163+, FOXP3+, and PD-L1), treatment response, and survival were evaluated. Public scRNA-seq datasets were used for complementary exploratory analysis of NOTCH3-associated transcriptional patterns. Results NOTCH3-high expression was associated with shorter overall survival, lower CD8+ TIL density, higher CD163+ tumor-associated macrophage density, lower chemotherapy response, and higher platinum resistance. High nutritional risk and hypoalbuminaemia were also associated with an immune-excluded phenotype after adjustment for clinicopathological covariates. The combined NOTCH3-high/NRS-2002 ≥ 3 subgroup had the poorest observed clinical outcomes. In the scRNA-seq analysis, epithelial cells showed the highest NOTCH3-related signature scores, and JAG1 showed the strongest co-expression with NOTCH3 among the evaluated ligands. These findings are associative and do not establish functional ligand-receptor signaling or a causal nutrition-mediated mechanism. Conclusion High NOTCH3 expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, adverse treatment response, and poorer survival in ovarian cancer. Nutritional risk identifies an additional clinically relevant correlate of immune and survival outcomes. The observational clinical design and exploratory public scRNA-seq analysis do not establish causality; functional validation and prospective studies are required before specific nutritional or NOTCH3-targeted interventions can be recommended.

papers.title: Safeguarding functionality of ATMPs: in-depth characterization of cryopreserved GMP-compliant nTreg products for therapeutic use.
papers.authors: Zhong T, Hartl C, Müller AT, Stüwe I, Lugo S, Yang M, Guerra GM, Chen Z, Hoffmann H, Münch S, Heinrich F, Durek P, Neumann N, Kaiser D, Fritsche E, Amini L, Springer J, Mashreghi MF, Polansky JK, Reinke P, Römhild A.
papers.abstract: Introduction Regulatory T cell (Treg) therapy has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring immune tolerance. However, its broader clinical implementation requires cryopreservation strategies that reliably preserve the biological integrity of therapeutic Treg products during Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) manufacturing. The feasibility of reduced dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) cryopreservation, including in our previous study, has been demonstrated. Yet its effects on the functional, metabolic, epigenetic, and molecular characteristics of therapeutic natural Treg (nTreg) products remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated the biological responses of GMP-compliant nTreg products to cryopreservation and determined whether reducing DMSO from 10% to 5% preserves key product characteristics after thawing. Methods Human GMP-compliant CD4 + CD25 + FOXP3 + nTreg products were cryopreserved using serum- and xeno-free formulations containing DMSO at different concentration. Fresh and cryopreserved cells were evaluated immediately (0 h) and 24 h after thawing by integrated viability, phenotypic, functional, metabolic, FOXP3 Treg-specific demethylation region (TSDR) analysis, and single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses. Results High-resolution respirometry demonstrated a transient mitochondrial activation following cryopreservation, while TSDR analysis confirmed maintenance of epigenetic lineage identity. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling revealed modest, donor-dependent responses to cryopreservation, with no significant differentially expressed genes between the 10% and 5% DMSO conditions under the predefined criteria. Single-cell chromatin-accessibility analysis showed broadly comparable accessibility-defined population architecture and preservation of accessibility at the assessed Treg lineage-associated loci FOXP3, IKZF2, and IL2RA . Reduction of DMSO to 5% in cryopreservation attenuated delayed cellular impairment, while maintaining phenotypic purity, cytokine quiescence, suppressive function, TSDR status, and high viability across 0 h and 24 h after thawing. Conclusion This study provides biological insight into the cellular responses of therapeutic Tregs to cryopreservation, while demonstrating that reduced DMSO cryopreservation preserves the investigated phenotypic, functional and molecular charactersitics of GMP-compliant nTreg products. By minimizing cryopreservation-associated cellular stress and reducing DMSO exposure to patients, this study supports the clincial applicability of reduced-DMSO cryopreservation within the investigated GMP manufacturing workflow, and may facilitate future implementation of cryopreserved Treg products by providing greater flexibility for product release, storage, and distribution.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: A cuproptosis-related gene signature and the protective role of CDKN1A in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Wang N, Chang W, Xu J, Guo F.
papers.abstract: Background Sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with high mortality, and reliable molecular biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to identify candidate cuproptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers and investigate the protective role of CDKN1A. Methods Differentially expressed genes from GSE10474 were intersected with cuproptosis-related genes, followed by functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, and machine learning using LASSO, random forest, and support vector machine algorithms. The resulting signature was evaluated in GSE32707 and GSE66890. Immune infiltration and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were performed, followed by experimental evaluation of CDKN1A overexpression in LPS-stimulated alveolar epithelial cells. Results An eight-gene signature comprising CDKN1A, MNDA, TREM1, ACP6, APOO, CHPT1, PIAS3, and SNRNP35 was identified. The models achieved AUCs of 0.786-0.886 in the training cohort and 0.654-0.745 in the validation cohorts. Immune analyses revealed dataset-dependent alterations in immune cell populations. CDKN1A overexpression attenuated LPS-induced cytotoxicity, improved cell viability and tight junction protein expression, modulated cuproptosis-related markers, reduced intracellular copper and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential. Conclusion The eight-gene signature represents a candidate diagnostic tool for sepsis-induced ARDS. CDKN1A overexpression is associated with protection against LPS-induced alveolar epithelial injury and modulation of cuproptosis-related and mitochondrial markers. Further mechanistic and prospective clinical validation is required.

papers.title: Multiplex immunohistochemistry in multiple myeloma: principles, spatial profiling applications, and emerging frontiers in immuno-oncology.
papers.authors: Zhou D, Guo X, Wang C, Bi L.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) progression and therapeutic resistance are dictated by the bone marrow microenvironment (BMME). Conventional single-marker immunohistochemistry (IHC) cannot resolve the complex cellular neighborhoods, non-cellular signaling networks, and spatial exclusion patterns that characterize this disease. Multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) and allied high-plex spatial imaging technologies now enable simultaneous visualization of 6 to over 60 protein targets on a single formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) section while preserving tissue architecture. This review first establishes a rigorous technical foundation by reclassifying mIHC and related high-dimensional imaging platforms according to their detection readout modality-fluorescence spectral unmixing/tyramide signal amplification (TSA) cyclic staining, DNA-barcode cyclic hybridization, metal-isotope mass spectrometric imaging, and regional-photolysis digital spatial profiling-and by clarifying several long-standing technical misconceptions (e.g., the historical relationship between PhenoCycler and Vectra Polaris, the cyclic nature of the Opal/TSA workflow, and the true elution chemistry of CODEX and t-CyCIF). We then present an expanded, bone-marrow-specific horizontal comparison of mIHC against flow cytometry, mass cytometry (CyTOF), imaging mass cytometry (IMC)/multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI), and spatial transcriptomics. Building on this technical scaffold, we organize the biological and clinical applications of mIHC along the natural disease continuum-monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) → smoldering myeloma (SMM) → newly diagnosed MM (NDMM) → post-treatment residual disease → relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) → extramedullary disease (EMD)-integrating T-cell, stromal, myeloid, and NK-cell compartments together with cytokine networks, metabolic competition, and bone-remodeling signals. We further delineate realized multimodal integration paradigms (mIHC combined with spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, digital spatial profiling, and artificial intelligence) and, separately, the technical, economic, and workflow bottlenecks-including spectral overlap, antibody cross-reactivity, turnaround time, cost, and the choice between bone marrow clot and decalcified trephine specimens-that currently constrain clinical translation. As methodological workflows for decalcified bone marrow specimens mature, mIHC is transitioning from a research tool to a critical component of precision immuno-oncology, offering actionable insights for overcoming CAR-T resistance and improving risk stratification.

papers.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
papers.authors: Grosso R, Ahmed SK, Li S, Wong-Beringer A.
papers.abstract: Background Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR). Materials and methods Murine Kupffer cells (KCs) were infected with live or heat-killed MRSA and treated with study compounds alone or in combination with vancomycin. Intracellular bacterial clearance was assessed at 0, 10, and 24 h post-treatment. KCs were challenged with heat-killed SA when evaluating compound immunometabolic activity: ROS generation using dihydroethidium fluorescence, TNF-α and IL-10 production by ELISA, and mitochondrial biogenesis markers (PGC-1 α, TFAM, mtDNA) by qRT-PCR, and MitoTracker assays. The role of 67LR mediating immunometabolic action was investigated by receptor disruption and binding studies via computational docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Results MCC-2 enhanced KC-mediated intracellular MRSA clearance by 1.07 log CFU reduction when combined with vancomycin compared to vancomycin alone. Enhanced clearance was accompanied by up to a 269% increase in ROS generation, a 3.4-fold increase in the TNF-α/IL-10 ratio, and a 25% increase in mitochondrial mass. Receptor disruption and binding studies suggest that MCC-2 activity is mediated partially via 67LR. MCC-4 showed similar mitochondrial activating effects as MCC-2 but was devoid of any antibacterial or immune enhancing activity. Discussion MCC-2 demonstrates promise for further development as an adjunct candidate to antibiotic therapy given its immunometabolic action in enhancing macrophage antimicrobial function while restoring mitochondrial competence through the putative target, 67LR.

papers.title: Causal Associations of Perturbational Phenotyping of Human Blood Cells and CHB: a Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.authors: Chen S, Chen C.
papers.abstract: Background The dynamic interaction between the hepatitis B virus (HBV) and the host's inflammatory response plays a key role in determining the extent of hepatic injury and disease progression. This study aimed to elucidate the causal relationships among perturbational phenotypes of human blood cells, immune cell dynamics, and chronic hepatitis B infection (CHB) and to further validate these immune traits at the single-cell transcriptional level. Methods This study systematically summarized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) investigating 91 perturbational phenotypes of human blood cells in relation to CHB. Furthermore, a mediator Mendelian randomization analysis was performed to assess the potential mediating roles of immune cells in the causal framework linking perturbational phenotypes of human blood cells to CHB. To validate key MR-derived immune features, single-cell RNA-seq data from CHB patients and healthy controls were analyzed to delineate immune cell populations and characterize cell-state alterations. Results The analysis identified one perturbational phenotype of human blood cells that showed a causal association with CHB in individuals of European ancestry. This phenotype involved the eosinophil perturbation response, represented by the side scatter median of eosinophil 1 at baseline, measured using WDF dye. The findings suggest that this response mediates CHB risk through CD33 expressed on CD33br HLA-DR+ CD14dim cells. Two additional perturbational phenotypes of human blood cells were causally related to CHB: neutrophil perturbation response (neutrophil 2/neutrophil 4 ratio in response to water perturbation measured by WDF dye) and platelet perturbation response (side scatter standard deviation of platelets in response to captopril perturbation measured by WNR dye). The neutrophil perturbation response influenced CHB risk through Mo MDSC AC, HLA-DR on CD14+ CD16- monocytes, and HLA-DR on CD14+ monocytes. The platelet perturbation response mediated CHB risk through Sw mem%B cells, secreting Treg %CD4 cells, CD25++ CD8br %T cells, and CD28+ CD45RA- CD8br %CD8br cells. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis further confirmed these MR findings by showing expanded inflammatory monocytes and MDSC-like cells, increased cytotoxic and regulatory T-cell activity, and reduced switched memory B-cell signatures in CHB. Conclusions This study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal relationship between perturbational phenotypes of human blood cells and CHB, indicating that immune cells may act as intermediaries in mediating this association. The integration of MR and single-cell profiling strengthens the biological plausibility of these pathways and highlights key immune states involved in HBV persistence and disease progression.

papers.title: Mendelian Randomization Identifies NPC1 as a Genetically Supported Protective Factor in Preeclampsia.
papers.authors: Song M, Wang J, Cao J, Li W, Jiao B, You X.
papers.abstract: Background This study aimed to identify ARGs associated with preeclampsia and to evaluate whether systemic inflammatory mediators genetically linked to ARG expression contribute to disease susceptibility. Materials and methods Placental transcriptomic data (GSE75010) were used to identify differentially expressed ARGs, followed by machine learning-based gene prioritization. A molecular diagnostic model was constructed as a screening tool and validated using GSE35574. Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were then performed using large‑scale genome‑wide association study datasets from eQTLGen and FinnGen Release 12 to investigate genetically supported associations between ARG expression and preeclampsia risk. A two‑step MR framework was applied to evaluate the mediating role of systemic inflammatory cytokines. Results Differential expression analysis identified 55 ARGs associated with preeclampsia. Random forest analysis further prioritized 24 feature ARGs, which were used to construct a diagnostic model with good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.87). Among these genes, 11 with available cis-eQTL instruments were further analyzed by Mendelian randomization. MR analyses revealed that higher genetically predicted ATG16L1 expression was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia, whereas higher genetically predicted ATG12 and NPC1 expression were associated with a reduced risk of preeclampsia. Two-step Mendelian randomization mediation analysis demonstrated that interleukin‑13 (IL‑13) partially mediated the association between genetically predicted NPC1 expression and preeclampsia risk, accounting for 16.57% of the total effect. Discussion This study provides genetic evidence linking autophagy-related pathways to preeclampsia susceptibility, with NPC1 as a candidate associated with lower risk, partly via IL-13-mediated immune modulation, highlighting the autophagy-inflammation axis for future research.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Machine Learning Reveal Oxidative Stress Hubs and Therapeutic Targets in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
papers.authors: Zhang SF, Xie WW, Li YX, Zhang YQ, Jin YR, Du YF.
papers.abstract: Background Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that oxidative stress is involved in its pathophysiology. This study explored oxidative stress-related mechanisms in IBS-D and screened potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrative bioinformatics analysis. Methods Transcriptomic datasets from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI)-Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were analyzed using integrative bioinformatics approaches to identify oxidative stress-related core genes in IBS-D. Eight potential biomarkers were identified and evaluated for diagnostic performance via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Among these, the key gene ACO2 was further investigated using Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG)-based gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune correlation analyses to explore the association between ACO2 expression and disease-related biological processes. In addition, the eight target proteins were used for reverse screening of potentially therapeutic traditional Chinese medicines and their active compounds. Results In total, 206 oxidative stress-related genes were identified, with predominant enrichment observed in mitochondrial energy metabolism and cellular stress-response pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) signaling. The eight potential diagnostic biomarkers demonstrated robust diagnostic performance (area under the ROC curve (AUC) = 0.896) in distinguishing IBS-D patients from healthy controls. Notably, ACO2 emerged as a key hub gene associated with distinct metabolic and immune-related pathway enrichment profiles. In parallel, a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory network centered on ACO2 was established, providing additional insight into its potential post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, reverse screening based on the eight target proteins identified luteolin, phillygenin, quercetin, and wogonin as candidate active compounds from Forsythia suspensa . Molecular docking further indicated favorable binding affinity between these compounds and the biomarker proteins. Conclusions This integrative bioinformatics study identifies oxidative stress-related molecular signatures and potential biomarkers in IBS-D. Reverse screening and molecular docking further suggest that luteolin, phillygenin, quercetin, and wogonin from Forsythia suspensa may represent potential candidate compounds targeting these biomarkers. These findings provide a theoretical basis for further experimental validation.

papers.title: A clinically applicable nomogram for predicting recurrent spontaneous abortion using coagulation and autoimmune markers.
papers.authors: Xie Y, Huang P, Gao X, Chen X, Yu C, Mu H.
papers.abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a risk prediction model for recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) by integrating thrombus markers with anticardiolipin antibody (ACA) and antinuclear antibody (ANA) indicators. Methodology Clinical data of 159 RSA patients (June 2021-June 2022) and 178 healthy controls from Rui'an People's Hospital were retrospectively analyzed. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including coagulation markers and autoantibodies, were analysed. Predictor selection was performed using a consensus approach combining univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and Random Forest feature importance. Multivariate logistic regression was subsequently used to identify independent predictors. Machine learning models were developed and evaluated using a 70:30 train-test split with 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and calibration metrics. Results Six independent predictors were identified: protein S, protein C, antithrombin-III (AT-III), fibrinogen (FIB), ACA-IgG, and ANA status. Reduced levels of natural anticoagulants (protein S, protein C, and AT-III) were associated with increased RSA risk, whereas elevated FIB and ACA-IgG levels and ANA positivity were significant risk factors. The Random Forest model demonstrated the best performance with an AUC of 0.765 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.665-0.851), sensitivity of 60.4%, and specificity of 75.9%. The model showed good calibration (Brier score 0.199). A nomogram based on logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.700. Conclusions A combined biomarker model integrating coagulation and immune parameters provides moderate-to-good predictive performance for RSA. This clinically applicable tool may facilitate early risk stratification and individualized management, although external validation is required before routine implementation.
